turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung protested that he did not want to hear such talk, that O-lan's condition was already too grave to be thinking of such things, and that he wanted her to rest and recover.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan that he would marry the maid, as she had always wished, and that he would make her happy in the house, and that she could rest easy knowing that he and his wife would take care of her and his father.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked, in a barely audible voice, if the eldest son was really certain he wanted to marry her, and if O-lan was truly content with the thought of their marriage

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked O-lan if she truly believed that the eldest son wanted to marry her, and if O-lan's approval was the only reason he had agreed to do so

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at the eldest son, her eyes filled with a deep sadness, and told him that she knew he was taking on a great responsibility, and that she was not just concerned about her own happiness, but about the well-being of the entire family

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung with a calm, determined gaze and asked if he had truly considered the future of their family without her, and if he knew how to provide for them in the difficult times that were to come

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked Wang Lung if he was truly confident in his son's ability to provide for her and the family, and if he had any doubts about their marriage

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked Wang Lung if he truly believed that his son was worthy of a wife, and if he thought she would be happy with such a husband

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she had seen the maid's doubts and that she knew the eldest son was worthy of a wife, but that the family's future was uncertain and that she worried for their well-being

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that the eldest son was strong and capable, and that the family would prosper under his care, but he could see the worry in O-lan's eyes and knew that she was not so easily reassured.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid told O-lan that she was sorry to cause worry, but she could not help but think of the difficulties that lay ahead for her husband and the family

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she must not worry, that he had worked hard to build a life for their family and that he would continue to provide for them, no matter what the future held.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would not let her concerns consume her, that she must rest and focus on her own recovery, and that he would take care of everything else, including the future of their son.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked O-lan if she could do anything to ease her worries, her voice barely above a whisper as she spoke, her eyes cast downward in respect

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would arrange for the eldest son to be married as soon as possible, so that she could see the family's future secured before she passed away

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told the eldest son that he must prepare himself for the responsibilities of marriage and family, and that he would need to be strong for their mother's sake

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son told O-lan that he would do his best to make his mother happy, and that he would be a good husband and father, just as his father had taught him

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son told his mother that he would not leave her side, that he would stay with her until she felt better and could rest easy

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung to ensure that the eldest son's bride was a good woman, someone who would take care of him and their mother

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan turned to the maid and asked if she had noticed any suitable young women in the village who might make a suitable match for their son.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
